fields.paulfranklin\n\n 2017-09-22 20:00\n\ndev:
It's been a long time since this "bug" was reported, in
2013 (a day after the tool was changed by Vasilii so that
it started failing). There have been many changes to the
date handler code, and specifically the DateParser class.

I believe that things like "parsing a date 'before May 1945'"
have worked for a long time. At any rate, they never failed
for me, whether I typed them in manually or used the tool.

In fact, when I glanced at the hundreds of failing dates, in
0007084:0031486 -- attached back in 2013 when this bug was created --
I don't see any failures listed for "before May 1945" dates,
normal years that is to say.

What did fail for me was the parsing of "slash dates" (also
called "double-dated" dates, I believe). The same as the
hundreds listed in the attached file. But only for dates with
no day, which started only when Vasilii modified the tool (to
add "0" days). Normal with-day dates had always passed the
tool, and still do, even for slashed years.

But on the off chance that some users might actually want
to type in (since they could always be entered using the date
editor dialog) dates like "1739/40" or "May 1722/3" or "1745/6
June" -- with or without any modifiers like "before" or "after"
or "calculated" or "from ... to ..." and so on, I have modified
the DateParser class to accept them. Or so I hope.

But I am leaving this bug open in case other people have
different results than I did, in my testing.

It's somewhat tedious to test that tool, time-consuming.
First you have to start gramps in some specific locale. In
my testing I used en_US and en_GB and sv_SE and fr_FR
and ru_RU. But it's not sufficient to just start gramps; it
must be started anew for each date format which is to
be tested, after selecting the format in Edit=>Preferences
Display tab (or the corresponding one in other languages).
Then a new, empty DB must be created, and only then is
the tool run.

For each of the locales/languages I made a DB with "ISO"
date-output format (even though I suspect that the code
is the same in all cases), also the second "Display" choice,
the "numerical" one. Then for all but Swedish I also made
DBs with some "dmy" and "mdy" date-output formats. For
Swedish I just selected one of the "ymd" formats (as none
exist in the new Swedish date handler with the year at the
end).

I viewed all the results in the "People" view, configured to have
the "Tags" column visible, and then I sorted that Tags column.
I then checked both the top and bottom of that column, to
make sure it said "Pass" in both cases (or the equivalent word
in the other languages), since if there had been any failures
the word Fail would have been in that column, either at the
top or at the bottom (depending on the language).

For all the locales, all the languages (I tested), all the date
formats (I selected), there were no failures reported by the
tool at all. All 3795 lines were always green.

So my conclusion is that the dates are correctly being
parsed, assuming I can believe that the tool is doing its
job.

But as I said, I am leaving this bug open in case others
wish to try things. Some other date format perhaps, or
a different locale/language, to get that date handler.

But the change I made is in the gramps50 repo now,
and so it will be in 5.0.0-alpha4 whenever it is released,
(if it is released, or some 5.0.0 "beta" if it isn't,) and
of course it will be in 5.0.0 also, when it is released.
